drhp.business: Halder Venture Limited is engaged in the manufacturing and sale of rice and edible oil as its principal businesses, with edible oil contributing approximately 73.88% of total standalone revenue. The Company also produces de-oiled rice bran as a by-product and has entered the branded aquaculture feed space, selling branded rice, edible oil and feed products to dealers, distributors and consumers across Eastern and North-Eastern India as well as select international markets.
drhp.expansion: The Haldia facility (acquired via the NCLT process) moved from acquisition to activation during FY 2025-26: a 33,000 MT tank farm and tin manufacturing/tin-filling/pouch-filling lines with cumulative capacity of 300 MT per day became operational, serving Odisha, West Bengal and the North East. A planned 500 MT refinery at Haldia is expected to be commissioned in the final quarter of FY 2026-27, deepening backward integration into refining. risks.note: Volatility in paddy, edible oilseed and crude edible oil prices, along with movements in fuel, packaging and freight costs, can affect input cost structures and margin stability in a highly competitive, price-sensitive consumer market.
risks.risk: Raw material and input cost volatility

risks.note: Approximately 60% of India's edible oil requirement is sourced from abroad; disruption in palm oil supply from Malaysia/Indonesia, a poor soybean harvest in Argentina, or adverse weather affecting sunflower production in Ukraine/Russia can sharply raise landed costs and compress refining margins — already evidenced in FY26 when crude sunflower oil import costs hit Rs.114/kg in September 2025 and refined sunflower oil reached Rs.170-175/litre at retail in early 2026.
risks.risk: High import dependence in edible oil

risks.note: Sudden changes in import duties, export restrictions, stock limits, minimum support prices or procurement/food-subsidy policies can materially alter market access, cost structures, inventory valuations and margins over short periods; export restrictions on rice and higher edible-oil import duty already compressed FY26 standalone economics.

The Company competes with local millers, regional brands, large national players and unorganised suppliers in both rice and edible oils; price-led competition in value-conscious markets can restrict the ability to pass on input cost increases and pressure operating margins.
risks.risk: Intense competition from organised and unorganised players

risks.note: Performance is closely linked to rural incomes, crop output, procurement policies and overall consumption sentiment; economic slowdown or adverse monsoon behaviour can impact demand and raw material availability across key product segments.
risks.risk: Dependence on rural incomes, crop output and monsoon behaviour

risks.note: When palm oil becomes expensive relative to soybean oil, the entire import basket shifts, affecting procurement planning, storage decisions and refining operations simultaneously.

Rising expectations around food safety, traceability, packaging quality and sustainability standards require continuous investment in processes, technology and compliance; failure to keep pace with evolving consumer or regulatory requirements (fortification, labelling, traceability, sustainable sourcing) could weaken competitive positioning over time.
